results.title: A Model-Based Approach to Risk Management for RVSAT-1: a Student Nano-satellite Project-Using SysML
results.abstract: In the recent past, the advancement of miniaturization and the revolutionary design philosophy have made nano-satellites the go-to platform for several commercial and scientific missions to low Earth orbit. The leverage for accommodating failures has thus reduced expeditiously, and analysis of mission-critical risks have assumed paramount importance to ensure the optimum performance of the system in its operating environment. However, from the Systems Engineering Methodology point of view, considerable nano-satellite projects continue to follow the conventional approach of Document-Based Systems Engineering. This approach involves the development of a Risk Response Matrix (RRM) to identify and categorize a risk based on its severity and likelihood. However, interpreting the risks associated with a nano-satellite through elaborate and esoteric documentation is maladroit and has quite a few pitfalls, the predominant ones being: the ineffective capturing of risks from a system point of view and a superficial understanding of how these risks affect other subsystems and subcomponents, apart from involving a substantial amount of book-keeping. To obviate these shortcomings, this paper expedites a novel idea of implementing a Model-Based Approach to assess and manage the risks faced by RVSAT-1, a student nano-satellite project, using SysML. The crux of the idea proposed is to represent the risks involved at the system and subsystem level as a model in SysML which depicts factors like risk severity and likelihood in a unique colour scheme based on a 'risk cube display'. Certain aspects such as consequences, risk ownership, mitigation and contingency plans too can be represented lucidly. Though developed for RVSAT-1, a student nano-satellite, this approach can be utilized for other complex systems as well. The proposed model for risk management enables ease of access and optimization, allowing the systems engineers to focus on value added tasks and ensure that a balanced approach is adopted towards managing risks. Through these proposed risk models, unprecedented levels of systems understanding can be achieved through integrated analytics, coalesced with a model-centric technical baseline. They can be used to intuitively assess and manage risks with great rigor and precision, contrary to the conventional document-based approach. © 2022 IEEE.

results.title: Open-source CubeSat MBSE Approach to Address Traceability: Power Subsystem
results.abstract: The benefits of using Model-based System Engineering (MBSE) approaches for the development of projects go beyond just replacing document-centric methods. MBSE is expected to aid in the ability to manage complexity and capture knowledge. By using MBSE approaches on CubeSats this paper aims to address notions of traceability and how system models can be used to verify the fulfillment of requirements. This work is carried out in Papyrus, an open-source model-based engineering tool, and builds on existing studies regarding CubeSats system models. The development of these sorts of models can benefit future CubeSat developers by reducing design time and cost. These models can also be used in an academic setting to facilitate learning about CubeSats and their design process. In this paper, a CubeSat power subsystem SysML model is presented, while the notion of traceability is introduced by the creation of a specific profile for model assumptions and a java code that allows visualizing the impacts of the change of one or more parameters of the CubeSat model. The model proposed in this paper contains key information about a system, such as requirements, structure, behavior, and analysis. This model-based approach for CubeSat subsystems helps to visualize and understand what is needed for the design of a CubeSat power subsystem, while guaranteeing that the designers are clearly aware of which requirements are being met and which are not. © 2023 IEEE.

results.title: Effective Model-Based Systems Engineering framework for academic nanosatellite project management and design
results.abstract: Nanosatellites, as a standardized Space research project with fast and cost-effective development possibilities, have enabled universities in a growing number of emerging countries to develop a wide range of space missions in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). This paper aims to contribute to research efforts to improve the success of university nanosatellite missions using Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) to facilitate the initial project management and design phases. The proposed model-based approach is the result of experience gained from the MASAT1 project, a Moroccan university nanosatellite, and it is based on an architectural framework that allows the system to be described via a set of views. The management and design process is based on a reference framework based on existing standards such as ESA’s European Cooperation for Spatial Standardization (ECSS). The choice fell on the Systems Modeling Language (SysML) for the MBSE implementation with the future goal of developing executable SysML Modeling approaches. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Council of European Aerospace Societies 2024.
